Answer: F
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates dextrocardia (heart on the right) and a gastric bubble on the right, confirming situs inversus totalis. In Kartagener's syndrome with situs inversus, the anatomical orientation is mirrored, so bronchiectatic changes are typically more pronounced on the left side (the morphological right lung), which aligns with the increased opacity and markings seen in the left lower zone of this image.
